euler-product.statement: where the real part of s is greater than one, the zeta function is the product over all primes p of the reciprocal of (1 minus p to the power minus s)

func-eq.statement: the completed function (s(s minus 1) over 2) times pi to the power minus s over 2 times gamma(s over 2) times zeta(s) is entire and equals its own reflection: xi(s) equals xi(1 minus s) — the functional equation

nozero-s1.statement: the zeta function has no zero when the real part of s is greater than one: each euler factor 1 minus p to the power minus s is nonzero there since p to the power minus s has modulus below one, and the product converges

num-zeros.statement: the first nontrivial zero of zeta is at height 14.1347, to four decimals — the next three at 21.0221, 25.0109 and 30.4249 — and the first ten to the thirteenth zeros have been verified to lie on the critical line: a numerical check, not a proof

pnt.statement: the prime number theorem: the chebyshev psi of x is asymptotic to x — in the logarithmic sense the primes are distributed like the integers

riemann.statement: every nontrivial zero of zeta has real part exactly one half — the nontrivial zeros are those not at a negative even integer; they are claimed to lie exactly on the critical line

rv-count.statement: the number of nontrivial zeros with height at most T is (T over 2 pi) times log(T over 2 pi) minus (T over 2 pi), with an error of order log T — the riemann-von mangoldt counting formula

s-of-t.statement: the sharp counting formula: N of T equals (T over 2 pi) log(T over 2 pi) minus (T over 2 pi) plus 7 over 8 plus S of T plus o of 1, where S of T is 1 over pi times the argument of zeta on the critical line at height T, and S of T is order at most log T

trivial-zeros.statement: zeta is exactly zero at every negative even integer: zeta of negative 2k is zero for every integer k at least one — the trivial zeros, zeroed by the sine factor sin(pi k) in the functional equation form

von-mangoldt.statement: the von mangoldt function is the log of p when the argument is a power of the prime p and zero otherwise; the chebyshev psi is its sum over the argument up to x

zeta-cont.statement: the zeta function continues to a meromorphic function on the whole plane; its only singularity is a simple pole at s = 1 with residue 1

zeta-series.statement: the zeta function is the sum over all n of n to the power minus s, and it converges when the real part of s is greater than one

reflect.statement: the symmetry of xi reflects zeros: a nontrivial zero s has 1 minus s as a nontrivial zero, with the same multiplicity

strip.statement: every zero of zeta either lies at a negative even integer or lies strictly inside the critical strip: a nontrivial zero has real part between zero and one — a zero past one would reflect to a zero past the left edge, forcing it to a trivial zero, and a zero at or past the left edge is trivial by the same reflection
